tagline: A dense, fast-moving European side district with strong community roots — popular street markets, local eateries, and a predominantly working-class character that keeps prices honest.

items.name: GOP Lokantalari
items.description: A concentration of unpretentious lokanta restaurants serving generous portions of traditional Turkish food at some of the lowest prices in the city.

items.name: Simitçiler ve Poğaçacılar
items.description: Street vendors and small bakeries selling simit, poğaça, and börek all day. A classic Istanbul working-class breakfast on the move.

items.name: Gaziosmanpaşa Semt Pazarı
items.description: One of the larger weekly street markets on the European side — fresh produce, clothing, and household goods at very competitive prices.

items.name: Geleneksel Kahvehaneler
items.description: Traditional coffee houses where locals play backgammon and socialise — a window into old-Istanbul neighbourhood life.

tips: Gaziosmanpaşa is well connected by metro (M7) and bus to the city centre.
One of the most affordable districts in Istanbul for both renting and eating out.
The local market is worth visiting for fresh produce even if you don't live here.
Less tourist-facing than central districts — a genuinely local Istanbul experience.
